profile.summary: Novae is a graph-based foundation model for spatial transcriptomics. It takes a spatial dataset at single-cell or spot resolution, builds a graph of neighbouring cells, and outputs a representation of each cell in its spatial context, which is used to assign spatial domains zero-shot across gene panels, tissues and technologies, with batch-effect correction built in.

summary_quotes.text: Novae is a deep learning model for spatial domain assignments of spatial transcriptomics data (at both single-cell or spot resolution). It works across multiple gene panels, tissues, and technologies.
a graph-based foundation model that extracts representations of cells within their spatial contexts

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Novae computes the spatial neighbours of each cell and learns cell representations with self-supervision on these graphs, a method adapted from SwAV. Representations are assigned to learned prototypes, which the documentation describes as elementary spatial domains; batch information is used only during training. The default human model's configuration sets 10 layers, 16 heads, hidden size 128, embedding size 512, output size 64 and 512 prototypes, with neighbourhood views of 2 hops.
sections.source_locator: README.md: Overview and Usage; docs/faq.md; novae-human-0 config.json

quotes.text: Illustration of the method behind Novae (self-supervision on graphs, adapted from [SwAV](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.09882))
each prototype can be interpreted as an "elementary spatial domain"
The batch information is used only during training (`fit` or `fine_tune`)

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Pretrained models on Hugging Face: novae-human-0 (the default for human tissues), novae-mouse-0 and novae-brain-0, each with 32,041,793 parameters, all created on 10 September 2024; and novae-scConcept-multi-species, with 3,124,983 parameters, created on 19 June 2026. The README announces a new improved model with a tutorial at a novae_scConcept page; it does not name the Hugging Face repository. A novae-test repository also exists. A result should name the model repository, its revision and the novae package version.
sections.source_locator: Hugging Face API responses; README.md: Recent updates

quotes.text: We added a new improved model

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Zero-shot or fine-tuned spatial domain assignment, batch-effect correction across slides, analysis of spatially variable genes and pathways, and architecture analysis of tissue slides; an optional multimodal mode uses H&E image embeddings.

quotes.text: (ii) analysis of spatially variable genes and pathways, and (iii) architecture analysis of tissue slides
Novae will use multimodal mode **if and only if** you ran `novae.compute_histo_embeddings` and `novae.compute_histo_pca`

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Graph-based foundation model for spatial transcriptomics.

quotes.text: Graph-based foundation model for spatial transcriptomics data

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Model over spatial neighbour graphs (the README calls it graph-based) trained with self-supervision on graphs adapted from SwAV, with prototypes. novae-human-0 config: 10 layers, 16 heads, hidden 128, embedding 512, output 64, 512 prototypes.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An AnnData of spatial transcriptomics with spatial neighbours computed; raw counts are normalised and log-transformed automatically when adata.X.max() > 10.

quotes.text: it will consider you have raw counts if `adata.X.max() > 10`, and then it will run `sc.pp.normalize_total` and `sc.pp.log1p`

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Cell representations in spatial context and assigned spatial domains, nested in a hierarchy.

quotes.text: constructs a nested hierarchy of spatial domains

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 32,041,793 each for novae-human-0, novae-mouse-0 and novae-brain-0; 3,124,983 for novae-scConcept-multi-species (Hugging Face safetensors counts).

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Nearly 30 million cells across 18 tissues, according to the preprint abstract. The model cards list the dataset prism-oncology/novae.

quotes.text: Our model was trained on a large dataset of nearly 30 million cells across 18 tissues

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: novae-human-0, novae-mouse-0, novae-brain-0 and novae-scConcept-multi-species on Hugging Face (plus novae-test).

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Not stated as a token limit. The model works on neighbourhood graphs (n_hops_local and n_hops_view of 2 in the human model config).

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: Not stated. The model cards and Hugging Face metadata carry no licence field.
facts.source_locator: Model card; Hugging Face API responses

facts.label: Code licence
facts.value: BSD-3-Clause, from the repository LICENSE file (copyright 2024 Quentin Blampey).

facts.label: Access
facts.value: Code: https://github.com/prism-oncology/novae (pip install novae, also on bioconda). Weights: https://huggingface.co/collections/prism-oncology/novae (not gated).

strengths.text: Zero-shot domain inference across gene panels, tissues and technologies.

quotes.text: allowing Novae to perform zero-shot domain inference across multiple gene panels, tissues, and technologies

strengths.text: Batch-effect correction is built in, with a parameter to control over-correction when fine-tuning.

quotes.text: you can provide the `min_prototypes_ratio` parameter to control batch effect correction

strengths.text: Runs on CPU in minutes: the FAQ states 5-20 minutes on CPU or 30 seconds to 2 minutes on GPU for typical inference.

quotes.text: typically takes 5-20 minutes on a CPUs, or 30sec to 2 minutes on a GPU

strengths.text: Installable from PyPI or bioconda, with separate human, mouse and brain models.

limitations.text: No weights licence is stated on the model cards.
Model choice matters: separate human, mouse and brain models plus a newer multi-species model, with very different sizes.

run_guide.summary: Install novae, compute spatial neighbours, load the pretrained human model and assign spatial domains zero-shot.
prerequisites: An AnnData object of spatial transcriptomics loaded in Python as adata.
A GPU is optional; set accelerator to use one.

steps.title: Create an environment and install
steps.shell:
conda create --name novae python=3.13
conda activate novae
pip install novae
steps.explanation: The documentation's optional conda environment and PyPI install. This installs the current release, not the reviewed commit.

steps.title: Assign spatial domains
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
import novae

# adata must already hold your spatial AnnData object
# compute cell neighbors
novae.spatial_neighbors(adata)

# load a pre-trained model
model = novae.Novae.from_pretrained("prism-oncology/novae-human-0")

# compute spatial domains
model.compute_representations(adata, zero_shot=True)
model.assign_domains(adata)
EOF
steps.explanation: The README's minimal usage example wrapped in a heredoc by Rewire. It does not load data: add your own line that creates adata before the neighbours call.

outputs: Representations and spatial domain labels stored in adata. The README does not name the fields.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The README's example assumes adata is already loaded; no data loading line is given.

notes: The repository moved from MICS-Lab/novae to prism-oncology/novae (GitHub redirects). The Nature Methods article (doi 10.1038/s41592-025-02899-6) is not open in PMC; the preprint is on bioRxiv (doi 10.1101/2024.09.09.612009, https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.09.09.612009; version and PDF address not verified) and was not requested. Released dates are Hugging Face repository creation dates. The record description says graph attention; the sources read do not name the layer type.
